#141817. Breaking: Alguacil looks at Milan’s favouritism, respect and playing to win: “Life or death match”

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (429 w)

Breaking: Alguacil looks at Milan’s favouritism, respect and playing to win: “Life or death match”

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (429 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.
  • Sources indicate that for Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game.
  • If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

Sources indicate that for Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

“What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

Recent findings suggest that “We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”.

Both teams are struggling with injuries….

“Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

Recent findings suggest that “Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

According to recent reports, “He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”.

Latest Update: ‘Apology FC’: Manchester United fans make clear demand after Sporting referee ‘robbery’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans have it out at referee Szymon Marciniak and UEFA over a host of controversial decisions during their 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League.
  • According to recent reports, the 2022 World Cup final ref pointed to the spot for a soft Sporting penalty in the first half, though Luis Suarez’s spot kick was saved by Senne Lammens.
  • Amad Diallo thought he had equalised, only for his goal to be ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, which earned the midfielder a yellow card after some vigorous protests.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans have it out at referee Szymon Marciniak and UEFA over a host of controversial decisions during their 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League.

According to recent reports, the 2022 World Cup final ref pointed to the spot for a soft Sporting penalty in the first half, though Luis Suarez’s spot kick was saved by Senne Lammens. Minutes later Lammens went from hero to zero when rushing out of his goal and taking out Maximiliano Araujo for another penalty. Suarez made amends from 12 yards.

Amad Diallo thought he had equalised, only for his goal to be ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, which earned the midfielder a yellow card after some vigorous protests.

Man Utd received a penalty of their own early in the second half also bordered on soft; Lisandro Martinez going down very easily after Eduardo Quaresma’s clumsy challenge.

Bruno Fernandes converted and then two minutes later benefitted from a divot of his own creation, albeit inadvertently, to hand Man Utd the lead, when he low, driven shot flicked up off the pitch to beat keeper Kaique Pereira.

A chaos continued when a Lammens howler saw Sporting equaliser, the keeper failing to deal with a cross to allow Suarez to instinctively, and acrobatically, finish from close range.

And then, at the other end of the pitch, an extremely similar scenario occurred as Pereira palmed the ball into his own net at a Man Utd corner for what appeared to be the winner.

Sources indicate that referee Marciniak initially awarded the goal, but VAR ordered a pitchside review which saw Martinez and Patrick Dorgu penalised for a foul on the keeper. There was still time for a red card as Tielemans was shown a second yellow for a late, studs up challenge.

The performance stirred up plenty of frustrations among the fanbase, especially in light of Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool which was later overturned by the Premier League.

There were plenty of fans, both with an affiliation to Man utd and not, claiming a “robbery”.

A Man Utd fan noted one of the decisions “boiled his blood”, while others were left waiting for another apology after the Yoro debacle.

But one Man City fan saw things slightly differently, insisting very decision was “spot on”...

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have added another experienced Premier League centre-half to their list of targets ahead of the transfer window opening.

After leaking four goals in another humbling defeat at Anfield on Sunday, Mauricio Pochettino has inherited the worst defence in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor is remarked to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

Fulham’s Calvin Bassey emerged as a potential target last week, but the versatile defender is reported to be close to signing a contract extension with the London club.

According to talkSPORT, United have also identified Brentford’s Nathan Collins as a possible solution to a problem that has plagued successive managers.

The Red Devils also have maintained an interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite but he is likely to prove too expensive, given they are reported to have a budget of just £50million to work with.

Collins, 25, is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029 and would also command a significant fee.

While reinforcements would certainly aid United’s cause, former club captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville fear it is not just defenders their old side are in need of.

‘My worry for United’s defenders [is] they’re not getting great help,” stated Keane after the Anfield drubbing.

‘I don’t think they’re great individually the defenders and they’re certainly not great as a group. It’s not as if you’re going, ‘Lads, we’re not all great. But the four of us together, we can do a good job’.’.

Recent findings suggest that neville added: ‘Do you know something. You watch a lot of League Two football, Roy. I watch League Two every single week;.

‘I don’t see a lack of order like this in League Two like I do in the Premier League sometimes. Chelsea [in their 4-1 loss vs Leeds on Saturday] were the same.’.

Industry News: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ex-Manchester United star Ashley Young labelled the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak during Wednesday’s chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting as a “disgrace”.
  • Marciniak was at the centre of multiple controversial decisions in a dramatic 2-2 league phase tie in Lisbon, awarding three penalties, ruling out two Man Utd goals and sending off midfielder Youri Tielemans in stoppage time.
  • Upcoming Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino claimed that his side had been “punished” by the officials, going on to say that it was “impossible” to understand how the decisions were reached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-Manchester United star Ashley Young labelled the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak during Wednesday’s chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting as a “disgrace”.

Marciniak was at the centre of multiple controversial decisions in a dramatic 2-2 league phase tie in Lisbon, awarding three penalties, ruling out two Man Utd goals and sending off midfielder Youri Tielemans in stoppage time.

Upcoming Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino claimed that his side had been “punished” by the officials, going on to say that it was “impossible” to understand how the decisions were reached.

Young held a similar position, with the former winger left searching for words when speaking about Marciniak’s display.

The ex-United captain stated on BBC Radio 5 Live: “The referee’s performance was just simply… wow.

“The decisions that he gave… Youri Tielemans getting booked, to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

“The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the ‘keeper.

“The ‘keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”.

Recent findings suggest that united fans would have been further irked by the decision to rule out their potential late winner, as Sporting’s equaliser came in a similar fashion. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens dropped a high ball under light pressure, allowing Luis Suarez to convert with an improvised bicycle kick.

However, talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor believes the reaction to the refereeing controversies has been overblown.

Recent findings suggest that he said on Thursday morning: “Manchester United fans, just get on with it. You didn’t deserve to win the game.

Sources indicate that “Did the referee make a couple of mistakes? Yes, he did. But come on. Manchester United fans - first they’re moaning about the owners, next they’re moaning about chief executives, [Omar] Berrada, [Jason] Wilcox. Now it’s referees every game, it’s VAR every game.

According to recent reports, “How about - you didn’t deserve to win the game? The referee didn’t make Lisandro Martinez make a stupid challenge to give away the first penalty that gets saved.

“The referee didn’t make [Noussair] Mazraoui come in so tight to the centre-half and allow the [Sporting] left-back flying forward.

In a recent development, “The referee didn’t make Lammens come out to no man’s land. I don’t know what he’s doing. I don’t know what he’s going to achieve running out there.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens have chocolate wrists and drop the ball when no one is on him.”.

The draw with Sporting leaves United 19th in the Champions League table, with three games remaining in this season’s league phase.

Tielemans’ red card means the Belgian will miss their next European fixture - a home tie with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig on December 8.

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:37.

Preston North End play host to Norwich City on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that could move them outside of the relegation zone.

At a time when the home side sit in 22nd place in the Championship table, Norwich remain in 11th position despite their prolonged unbeaten streak.

While many questioned why Graham Alexander left a League One promotion bid with Bradford for a relegation scrap at Deepdale, the Preston legend is currently justifying his decision.

Seven points have been accumulated across the last three fixtures against Southampton, West Ham United and Cardiff City.

Preston had been heavy underdogs in all three contests, yet they came through that triple-header having conceded just the one goal.

Although Preston had to battle hard to earn a share of the spoils at West Ham on Saturday, they were ruthless in dispatching Cardiff by a 4-0 scoreline in South Wales three days later.

Despite remaining three points adrift of safety, confidence is growing at Preston ahead of facing one of the form teams in the division.

Such has been the upturn in Norwich's fortunes that they were disappointed to record a 1-1 draw at home to Queens Park Rangers in midweek.

Nevertheless, having won their previous five games, it extended their recent return to 16 points from a possible 18.

Philippe Clement's side remain with three points of sixth-placed Southampton, a position they will take having lost eight of their opening 11 league matches this season.

Norwich have scored 19 goals in eight away fixtures, the joint-best attacking record in the division, while they have won their most recent three contests away from Carrow Road.

Barring any fitness concerns, Preston boss Alexander is expected to name the same starting lineup from the Cardiff game.

Preston were 4-0 ahead before substitutions were first made in the 77th minute, and the same players should keep their places.

The likes of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson and Liam Gibbs are all expected to remain sidelined.

Meanwhile, Kenny McLean, Anis Ben Slimane, Oscar Schwartau and Jovon Makama are all in contention for opportunities in the Norwich XI.

Jacob Wright, Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden could be the players to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:.

Nicholls; Hughes, Lindsay, Offiah; Mills, Thompson, Docherty, Small; Devine, Moran; Burgzorg.

Norwich City possible starting lineup:.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Yongwa; Field, McLean; Brooks, Ven Slimane, Musaba; Makama.

Although Preston recorded the most eye-catching Championship result in midweek, it remains to be seen whether they can back that up against a team playing with Norwich's confidence. Therefore, we are backing the Canaries to come out on top, albeit in a match where Preston will continue to show their improvements under Alexander.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicky Butt believes that Liverpool will prove to be Arsenal’s main title challengers over the likes of Manchester City this season.

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Brighton had the chance to cut that lead to just three points, but a late Oli McBurnie brace saw them lose 2-0 to Hull City on Sunday.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

City will have the opportunity to eat into Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table when the two sides meet at the Emirates next week.

However, Butt does not expect them to last the course in this season’s title race, instead talking up Liverpool’s chances after their impressive 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday.

‘Any win for Liverpool against Man United or vice versa is massive,’ Butt mentioned on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘Forget the ten men or the level of the team they are playing against at the time. When Liverpool beat Man United or the other way around, it’s a massive result, especially for a latest manager.

‘It was only a couple of years ago that they won the league, so they’re not a bad team, and they’ve added well.

‘They are the only ones that I think can challenge Arsenal this year.’.

Paul Scholes, meanwhile, was less certain about Liverpool’s title chances this season, but admitted he was impressed by their start under Andoni Iraola.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s started off well, hasn’t he?’ Scholes noted. ‘I think it’s going to be gradual, but they have got the makings of a very good team.

‘And they haven’t half spent a few quid, they’ve got three £100m-plus players so you would expect them to be alright.’.

Liverpool will look to make it three league wins on the spin when they return to action next Sunday against local rivals Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Omar Marmoush has backed his "unbelievable" Tottenham team-mate Luca Williams-Barnett to have a "very significant future".

The teenager has impressed under Roberto De Zerbi in recent weeks, most notably scoring and assisting in their Premier League win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Aged 18 years and 51 days, Williams-Barnett became the second-youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

He also became the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start, behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d) and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Should he start and score against Sunderland on Sunday, he'd be the youngest player to score in his first two starts (18 years, 59 days).

The forward's breakthrough into the Spurs' first team was rewarded with a new contract, which is reported to be a five-year deal, and Marmoush believes the only way is up for the exciting winger.

"He is unbelievable," Marmoush told Sky sports about Williams-Barnett.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have ditched their traditional sky blue home kit for their Champions League tie against Napoli on Tuesday night.

Instead of their usual home strip, City will be wearing a ‘special edition’ orange kit which has been produced by Puma but also alongside the club’s ‘official style fashionwear partner’ CP Company.

Ahead of kick-off at the Etihad Stadium, City’s players also turned up in bright orange jackets to complement the limited edition kit.

In a statement released before the game against Napoli, City stated: ‘Manchester City have this evening debuted a special edition kit in collaboration with Club partners, PUMA and C.P. Firm.

‘The kit will be worn for select fixtures in the Champions League, and forms part of a wider collection that will be on sale globally from Tuesday 1 December.

‘There will also be an exclusive presale event for fans on Monday 30 November at the City Store in Medlock Square.’.

Meanwhile, Enzo Maresca has made five changes for his side’s Champions League game against Napoli.

From the side that started the 1-1 Premier League draw at home to Fulham on Saturday, Rayan Cherki, Enzo Fernandez, Josko Gvardiol, Matheus Nunes and Allan have all been brought into the starting line-up.

Abdukodir Khusanov, Ruben Dias, Iliman Ndiaye, Phil Foden and Jeremy Doku have all dropped to the bench.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.

Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.

Xabi Alonso is among several managers who appear to be assessing the versatile VfL Wolfsburg defender ahead of a potential transfer.

The Blues, Tottenham and Fulham are all 'monitoring' Kumbedi, while City Football Group have also been tracking his progress throughout the campaign, according to TEAMtalk.

The right-back moved to Germany from Lyon in August 2025, initially joining Wolfsburg on loan before the Bundesliga club activated their €6m purchase option.

Despite Wolfsburg suffering relegation to Bundesliga 2, Kumbedi opted to remain with the club and help them pursue an immediate return to the German top-flight.

His decision has not prevented his reputation from growing, with Zinedine Zidane handing him his first senior France call-up earlier this month following an injury withdrawal from the squad.

Kumbedi made his international debut against Italy at San Siro on November 12th, becoming the first Bundesliga 2 player to receive a France senior call-up since David Trezeguet in 2007.

Chelsea's interest in Kumbedi could make sense given the uncertainty surrounding their options at right-back.

Reece James' injury problems have created a significant headache for Alonso, with Pedro Neto having been deployed in a wing-back role and centre-back Josh Acheampong also shifted out to the right.

Malo Gusto's uncertain future at Stamford Bridge is another potential consideration, leaving Chelsea with reasons to explore the market for a specialist defender capable of providing greater depth and versatility.

European scouts are reportedly impressed by his pace, athleticism and stamina, while his ability to operate on either flank further adds to his appeal.

That versatility is particularly attractive to a side like Chelsea, who are seeking defensive reinforcements in 2027, with the French gem's performances over the coming months likely to remain under close scrutiny.

However, the west London side are not alone in their interest, with top-flight rivals Spurs, Fulham and City also monitoring the Frenchman.

His international breakthrough could make competition for his signature increasingly fierce, but Chelsea's need for greater stability and depth on the right makes this a potential transfer worth watching.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Raya was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw away to Newcastle United on Saturday evening.
  • The Spanish goalkeeper appeared to be in significant discomfort and has been unable to train since Arsenal’s game at St James’ Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta says David Raya will undergo more tests on his shoulder injury before Arsenal’s Premier League game against Manchester City on Sunday.

Raya was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw away to Newcastle United on Saturday evening.

The Spanish goalkeeper appeared to be in significant discomfort and has been unable to train since Arsenal’s game at St James’ Park.

Kepa Arrizabalaga took Raya’s place in goal for Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at home to Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

But Arteta admits Raya is still an injury doubt for Arsenal’s next Premier League fixture against City at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

Speaking ahead of kick-off against Dortmund, Arteta told Prime Sport: ‘Again, we need some more tests.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He’s evolving well. Obviously, we were very relieved with the news because we feared the worst. But we’ll have to wait and see.’.

When asked after his side’s 2-2 draw with Dortmund, Arteta added: ‘We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not in the next few weeks.’.

During his pre-match press conference on Monday, Arteta confirmed that Raya will not need to undergo surgery.

‘He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn’t look too serious and we need more tests tomorrow but it’s quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action,’ Arteta noted.

‘We were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

‘The doctor explained what happened but it’s quite technical and when you look at the action there doesn’t seem to be much, but the extent of the pain that he had and the pain he had was quite worrying.’.

Manchester City have been given an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges ahead of this weekend’s huge title clash with Arsenal.

City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018. The commission also found the Man City had made "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate" the investigation.

The club have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately rolled out with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should the appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League, all the while Man City‘s form on the pitch has suffered a dip.

Sources indicate that city have won just one of their last five games across all competitions, and have lost three of their last four in the Premier League to see their title hopes handed a huge blow. Arsenal is up next on Sunday in a game Erling Haaland has already described as their “toughest of the season”.

Amid the on-pitch struggles, financial expert Stefan Borson, who previously worked as a financial advisor to City, expects there to be clarity sooner rather than later over the club’s off-pitch concerns.

"We're told that it will be mid-December,” Borson mentioned, regarding the appeal hearing, on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan.

“Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th.

"It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time.

"I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season.".

Borson suggested a timetable may already have been agreed, with the Premier League keen to avoid further legal complications.

Sources indicate that "In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable. In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable.

"I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away.

Recent findings suggest that "The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan will make the trip to Greece with the hopes of turning a corner against Olympiacos after a rough start to their Europa League campaign.

It has been a tale of two competitions this season so far for Milan. In Serie A they are inside the top four and have won eight games out of 12, leading to suggestions of a Scudetto bid. However, in Europe they have lost three of four, and sit in the bottom eight.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that it means that they’ll have to be perfect to even be in with a chance of a top eight finish – given you’ve needed at least 15 points in the last two seasons. Nevertheless, a point and gaining a bit of momentum across all competitions would still be appreciated.

Game date: Thursday, November 26 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: Karaiskakis Stadium Referee: Chris Kavanagh (VAR: Bankes).

Industry observers note that as mentioned, things have been going quite well for Milan domestically. Sunday’s 5-1 victory against surprise package Frosinone was another example of the potential of this team, but there remains a necessity to find some consistency.

In a recent development, this is especially the case when it comes to the Europa League, in which the Rossoneri have been quire frankly awful. A 4-0 win against RB Salzburg in round two was the only glimmer of light, with the other three games being defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring.

As things stand right now, Milan would not even make the play-off spots as they sit outside the top 24. There is only one point in it and even eighth is only four points away, though the runway is getting shorter with only 12 points to play for.

The result of this is that Amorim is expected to name quite a strong side for the game, but we must start with the injury absences. The big doubt is Strahinja Pavlovic, who needs another check on a kidney stone problem despite playing 20 minutes off the bench against Frosinone.

Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano and Ruben Loftus-Cheek have all missed the past few games due to various issues and will not be available on Thursday either.

According to recent reports, on Tuesday, the news broke that Milan will be without Luka Modric, who felt a tweak in his right thigh during the last game. The Croatian will be given Thursday night to recover and potentially the Cagliari game too, with the hopes of having him back at the start of December. Then, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi have already been ruled out.

The other bit of news is that Fikayo Tomori returned to training on Wednesday, which is a massive boost given how thin the options are in defence, but it remains to be seen if the Englishman is deemed fit enough to play a part after his absence.

With the squad running quite thin, Amorim won’t have many options to rotate, nor does he have the luxury to with the standings.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, there will be one at the back, where Pervis Estupinan is expected to start. Mike Maignan starts behind Sankhoun Diawara and Koni De Winter, with Mario Gila at right-back again.

In a recent development, modric’s injury means Ardon Jashari will be given a chance on Thursday, and it’s one he must take. Alongside him, he’ll be covered with reliability from Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot, which should help.

Finally, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are expected to start on the flanks, with Goncalo Ramos through the middle.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Torriani, F. Terracciano, M. Cissé, Tomori, Perera, Comotto, Vos, Ossola, Hutchinson, Cisse, Menon.

According to recent reports, injuries & suspensions: Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Modric, Pavlovic, Camarda, Bartesaghi.

It has been revealed that olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

It has been revealed that the spending was almost totally offset by four substantial sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

It has been revealed that mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the newly introduced head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Industry observers note that olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

In a recent development, in the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey may be the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical challenges, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

In a recent development, AC Milan and Olympiacos have faced each other four times. Two came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19, which means that the meetings were almost 60 years apart.

In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

The most recent encounters were eight years ago as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

Industry observers note that ➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

In a recent development, ➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

It has been revealed that ➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

According to recent reports, ➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

According to recent reports, starting in midfield, the obvious choice here is Ardon Jashari. This has been called his game by the Italian media and it’s tough to disagree. If he’s going to have a future with the club beyond this season, a strong start tomorrow is imperative.

Recent findings suggest that the other obvious choice is Pervis Estupinan. The Ecuadorian is a late entry into the expected XI, despite reports linking him with a potential exit in January. Bartesaghi’s injury means he’ll be given a chance and maybe, just maybe, it’s not too late for him. Something of promise needs to be seen, though.

Recent findings suggest that with Milan lacking Modric in their midfield, it could allow someone like Remo Freuler to take the game by his pace. He’s got plenty of European experience and with the Rossoneri likely to rely on Jashari to set the pace, he may take the edge.

Industry observers note that then, if Leon Bailey starts, he’ll be the big threat of the night. Facing Estupinan and Diawara, he’ll have the opportunity to face a duo that have no relation yet. If he catches them out, it could be a long night for the Diavolo.

In a recent development, it’s been a real case of Jekyll and Hyde for Milan in the Europa League, to the point where it’s tough to call which side we’ll see. Logically, after such a heavy win at the weekend, the visitors should be coming away with three points.

Industry observers note that however, both teams aren’t brilliant defensively and it could become an open game as a result. Considering what’s at stake, though, the Rossoneri may just edge past the hosts, but it won’t be easy….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund told Manchester City fans ‘there is only one club in Manchester’ after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash on Tuesday night.

Hojlund scored the opening goal in the second half at the Etihad Stadiumbut City salvaged a 2-2 draw following Rayan Cherki’s equaliser in the 86th minute.

After scoring his first Champions League goal of the season with a brilliant low finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma, Hojlund celebrating in front of City’s supporters.

But before turning to the half way line, the Denmark international held up one finger and told the crowd: ‘There is only one club in Manchester’.

When asked about his celebration after the game, Hojlund stated: ‘Some good banter, you know.

Sources indicate that ‘There’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and obviously I have a past in Manchester United. That’s my club. Nothing against City but United is my home.’.

Former Red, Rasmus Hojlund scoring at the Etihad tonight:“There’s only one club in Manchester” 🔴⚪️⚫️😍 pic.twitter.com/mS5eQsMWRA.

Hojlund joined Manchester United in a £72 million deal from Atalanta in 2023 and spent two seasons at Old Trafford before his loan move to Napoli.

The 23-year-old then completed a £38 million permanent move to Napoli this summer as the Serie A club had an obligation to sign him after qualifying for the Champions League.

During his two seasons at United, Hojlund scored 26 goals in 95 appearances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:49.

Derby County and Watford square off at Pride Park on Saturday afternoon as two of the worst performing teams in the division.

While the Rams sit at the bottom of the Championship table, Watford are only five points ahead of them and with a head coach taking charge of his first Hornets match.

When Derby travelled to Molineux to face Wolverhampton Wanderers on Tuesday night, they would not have necessarily expected to earn anything from one of the form teams in the division.

However, despite having troubled Wolves during the opening half hour, the Rams succumbed to a 3-0 defeat and allowed their opponents to have the most shots (39) by any team in the Championship in 11 years.

John Eustace has now overseen 11 defeats in 17 league matches, and it is realistic to assume that he may be sacked if Derby lose this game.

In four of their last eight outings, Derby have conceded at least three goals, while they have only netted more than once in a fixture in 13 outings.

On a positive note, the East Midlands outfit did win their last contest at Pride Park, overcoming Bolton Wanderers by a 3-1 scoreline on November 6.

Meanwhile, Watford head into this encounter with former Romania and Legia Warsaw boss Edward Iordanescu in the dugout for his first game in English football.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

A quick glance at two contrasting stats sums up exactly where Arsenal’s shortcomings lie at the moment.

Mikel Arteta’s side are still in fine shape to progress straight through to the last 16 as one of the top-eight sides in the Champions League. Only the Gunners, holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid remain unbeaten in this season’s competition.

Industry observers note that however, it could have been so much better, after an extraordinarily wasteful display in the draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night. Arsenal registered 30 shots, but only four on target and they scored just once.

It should have been so much more for Martin Odegaard, too. He has registered only one assist in Europe this season, ranking him 45th in the competition for that metric.

And yet for expected assists, per FotMob, Odegaard ranks top across the entire Champions League. Above Nico Paz, who has five assists to his name, and Lamine Yamal, who has three.

Arsenal have had no glitch creating chances. Against Dortmund, Odegaard laid on nine of them, the most by any player in a Champions League match this season.

That was just the second time this decade that an Arsenal player has created more than five chances in a Champions League match. The other example? Odegaard against Napoli in September.

According to recent reports, the discourse around Odegaard is often hypercritical. That, to an extent, is understandable. He has been the captain and creative heartbeat of the team in a period in which, for all it has been successful, there have been ongoing questions surrounding the attack.

It is perhaps also a hangover from the last two seasons, when injuries hampered Odegaard and he was well off his best. Frustration towards him built and some minds appear to have been made up.

However, the criticism that he does not deliver consistently enough just does not hold up to scrutiny this season.

Man City get appeal verdict update ahead of Arsenal clash.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal.

Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as signing confirmed.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

From the moment Odegaard returned to the club in the summer after a strong World Cup with Norway, he has looked back to his best. That started with his sublime goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield and has continued since.

For all there have been some notable exceptions, Arsenal have on the whole played much better football this season. They have been far more free-flowing and fluid in attack.

It has been revealed that odegaard has been central to that. Along with his chance creation stats in Europe, Odegaard is also second for expected assists in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that he is taking more responsibility in front of goal, too. Odegaard is Arsenal’s top scorer this season and is only one league goal shy of his combined tally from the last two seasons.

Industry observers note that if there has been a dip in Arsenal’s attack from the start of this season, that is not down to Odegaard. Bukayo Saka, who was displaying far better goalscoring instincts, suffering a quad injury, and Kai Havertz’s performance levels dropping significantly are far more relevant explanations.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard.

Odegaard has been the most consistent forward player. It is not just the chances created or even the goals, but his influence in all facets of Arsenal’s game as almost an extension of Arteta on the pitch. He is the leader of the press, and that led to the winning goal against Liverpool at Anfield earlier this month.

According to recent reports, arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard. It is not an exaggeration to say that Viktor Gyokeres should have scored another three goals against Dortmund from chances created by Odegaard alone.

Recent findings suggest that the Gunners are not clinical enough but that is not the fault of the player creating the chances. Nor is it a coaching issue. Arteta could not have done more to deliver a win against Dortmund.

The problem is a personnel one. The quality of Arsenal’s attackers does not come close to matching the level in every other position in the squad. At least one top-class winger signing is required, along with a fresh striker.

Industry observers note that it was clear at the end of last season that significant upgrades were needed. Instead, Arsenal sold three forwards and signed only Christos Tzolis.

Recent findings suggest that that is the significant failure and where the fingers should be pointing. Not at Odegaard for occasionally taking too many touches or making a wrong decision on the counter.

Industry observers note that odegaard’s contract situation adds another factor to the debate over his role in the team. He is nearing the final 18 months of his current deal.

Talks have not yet begun over an extension, Odegaard revealed during the international break, but that should be a no-brainer for Arsenal.

That will require the club to make another significant financial commitment, following on from several other new contracts for key players, but it is still a far cheaper alternative to trying to sign a replacement of Odegaard’s quality.

Securing Odegaard’s future should be the club’s next top priority, swiftly followed by then delivering him the forwards he deserves.

The Ukrainian giants are this season playing their home European games in west London due to Russia's ongoing invasion of their home country, having in previous seasons staged their home games in Poland, Germany and Slovenia.

Industry observers note that the matches have attracted local and travelling Ukrainian football fans, along with thousands of rivals supporters as Greek side AEK Athens and Portuguese outfit Sporting came to town earlier this season. Real Madrid will visit at the end of January.

Wednesday night saw Fenerbahce as the visiting team, and the fanbase came in numbers.

Stamford Bridge was glowing red from the light of flares ahead of the game, while footage of supporters descending on west London and the surrounding Chelsea area spread across social media.

As the designated away team, Fenerbahce were allocated the 'Shed End' of Stamford Bridge, which is said to hold around 6,000 fans, but thousands more were seen across 'home' sections of the stadium.

The tickets went on general sale earlier in November, which allows any member of the "general public" to purchase.

Fenerbahce won the game 1-0 and, speaking after the game, Ismail Yüksek mentioned: “There were nearly 30,000 Fenerbahce fans in the stadium today.

According to recent reports, "You wouldn’t see anything like this at any other club in the world. They gave us incredible support. They were amazing. They gave us incredible strength. I dedicate this victory to them.

"From the first minute to the last, the team fought just as hard as our fans. We deserved this victory from start to finish.".

So to see how far we all are behind, besides Arsenal, they got to the Champions League final last season, you see City tonight, you see Villa lose, Liverpool lost a couple of weeks ago away to Fenerbahce.

According to recent reports, ‘I still think you’ve almost got four or five teams, Arsenal are one of them, the big teams in the Champions League. For the Premier League not to have more than one, considering we’ve got five in the competition and the funds they all have, it’s probably a bit disappointing and shows why Arsenal are favourites for the Premier League.’.

Meanwhile, Thierry Henry believes City’s run of form indicates that Maresca’s side could struggle to control the game against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

‘You have two teams who have to rectify two things at the weekend – Arsenal, like we’ve been saying recently, and Mikel Arteta has been saying, when you’re on top of a team, don’t let them come back to attack like we’ve seen in the last two games,’ Henry said.

It has been revealed that ‘If you go back to City, and I’ve said it since the beginning of the season, the balance of the team isn’t right. Simple as that.

‘They have quality, they have goalscorers who will bail them out, Rayan Cherki bailed them out tonight, but the cohesion of the team, the way they don’t stop counters, they don’t control the game on and off the ball like they used to.

‘That didn’t stop them losing games under Pep [Guardiola] but they were more in control of games.

‘You have two teams who have been dominating the league in the last two, three years. But I want to see an Arsenal team that’s going to dominate City, and they are there to be dominated.

According to recent reports, ‘But on the other side, it might be the day that City wake up. But if they play the same way they’ve been playing recently, being open and all over the place in midfield, it could be a long day.’.

Ahead of a do-or-die clash against Olympiacos for AC Milan in the Europa League, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

There’s still time for Milan to turn around their Europa League campaign, but so far, it’s been one to forget. Their successes in the league have often been reduced thanks to poor performances in midweek, and that cannot happen again.

After a dismantling of Frosinone at the weekend, Amorim’s side should be full of confidence and wholesale rotations are not expected in Greece tomorrow night. So, logically, that confidence should continue and there should be several reasons to feel hopeful of a result.

In a recent development, however, as we know, there have been similar feelings heading into Europe this season and the Rossoneri have often not followed up with performances of similar levels. Tomorrow must be different.

Speaking alongside Ardon Jashari, the Portuguese discussed the challenge his team will face tomorrow, as MilanNews relays.

Industry observers note that what do you ask of the team for tomorrow? More volume in attack? How do you proposal to support Ramos?

In a recent development, “It’s not about helping Ramos, but also Camarda and everyone up front. It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third. The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players.

“Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

In a recent development, “We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”.

How would you describe Olympiacos as a team?

Sources indicate that “Thank you for the welcome. They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do.

It has been revealed that “They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3; they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players. They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match.

Sources indicate that “Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”.

Does AC Milan’s growth also involve Europe?

It has been revealed that “To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe. That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan.

Sources indicate that “My compliments? I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way.

Industry observers note that “We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone. We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at major clubs. We have to be ready for this.

According to recent reports, “I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated. We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.

“I believe in all competitions, but if we can win them all, no. Scudetto? I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it. I won’t change for the compliments, because I’m waiting and so are you.

“You’re waiting [for criticism]. Tomorrow we have to win, because if we don’t… I’m ready for that.”.

Is football becoming dangerous for the mental and physical health of players and coaches?

Industry observers note that “It’s difficult to protect players considering the times we’re living in. Younger players will be more willing to live with criticism. It’s different from my reality. It’s difficult to control this.

According to recent reports, “When you asked me about GTA, I’d rather my players play every day rather than scroll through social media. What I mean is that we want more time between games. I’m talking about the product, not my life.

In a recent development, “I’m talking about the quality of the football product. I don’t know what Fabregas meant, but it’s the evolution of society, of football, which is a business, and we have to be ready.

“Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”.

You have a lot of experience as a player: what do you expect from the stadium tomorrow?

Recent findings suggest that “I know the atmosphere here. It’s incredible. It’s key for my players to have this experience, even though there’s no stadium more difficult to play in than San Siro. We have to be ready in these kinds of stadiums.

Sources indicate that “We lost 5-1 once, but I’m very focused on what we have to do, how we’ll start the match, I’m focused on these things. The atmosphere should be normal for these players, who are used to substantial events. We have to be competitive and ready.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09.
  • Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.
  • The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09.

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The latest manager's debut did not go to strategy, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Le Havre possible starting lineup:.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana.

Strasbourg possible starting lineup:.

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder.

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a massive future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

According to recent reports, ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

It has been revealed that but when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their substantial spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

‘I think at the very beginning he highlighted why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips noted when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a major game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

Pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

According to recent reports, ‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

Sources indicate that ‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

In a recent development, ‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11.

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier presently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

  • Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.
  • Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose in north London on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose in north London on Sunday.

It has been revealed that city are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Head coach Enzo Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few matches. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

Predicted Man City XI vs Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Fernandez, Anderson; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am demonstrates him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

He is at the moment without a club.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.
